newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude posts session low after NYMEX open.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude posts session low after NYMEX open.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures tumbled to new session lows in early afternoon trade on Friday as U.S. markets got off to a weak start, brokers said.
June Brent shed 13 cents to $18.16 a barrel by 1417 GMT, just two cents above the intraday low posted shortly after NYMEX dealing began.
Dealers said a combination of soft U.S. refined product prices and a weak technical picture was driving markets lower.
"We've seen a fair bit of selling of the gasoline and heating oil cracks in the U.S.," said one.
Breaks of support on Brent and gas oil fuelled the losses.
"On (June) Brent, $18.18 was a number to watch and we've gone through that and $167.75 (a tonne) on gas oil has also gone," said a broker.
May gas oil lost $4.50 to trade at $166.50 a tonne by 1427 GMT, just $1 above the low for the day.
NYMEX heating oil related losses were being compounded by slack demand in Europe, where much of the continent is basking in unusually high temperatures, and a narrower arbitrage to the Far East.
Dealers said they expected trading volumes to remain thin.
